Process & deliverables

From site question to usable output.

Agree the question and the deliverable first. Then plan, prepare, capture, process and hand over what your project needs.

Start your brief →See the five stages
Stock photo

After you agree the brief

Five stages, in the same order every time.

The technical method changes by project. The sequence does not.

Stock photo
  1. 01

    Plan

    Confirm the site, purpose, coverage, deliverable and any constraints.

  2. 02

    Prepare

    Review access, site information and the practical considerations before capture.

  3. 03

    Capture

    Fly the agreed area and collect the imagery or mapping data the brief needs.

  4. 04

    Process

    Prepare the agreed photographs, video, orthomosaic or 3D model.

  5. 05

    Deliver

    Hand over the agreed files.

Before capture

Define the question, coverage and handover before flying.

A short brief prevents wasted capture and keeps the output tied to the decision your team needs to make.

Start your brief →
Site
Where is the project and which area matters?
Question
What do you need to understand from the aerial view?
Output
Inspection imagery, mapping, a model, monitoring, photography or video?
Constraints
Are there access, timing or project considerations that affect capture?
Handover
Who will use the files and what do they need from them?

Common deliverables

Different formats answer different questions.

A useful deliverable is the one your project team can actually use.

Common deliverables and the services that produce them
DeliverableWhat it is forService
Inspection photographsDetailed aerial photographs of agreed roof, structure or site areas.Roof inspections →
Orthomosaic mapsA stitched 2D view of the site for planning, progress review and CAD overlay.RTK & 2D mapping →
Georeferenced 3D modelsInteractive models for remote inspection, measurement and CAD/BIM-related use.3D modelling →
Progress recordsConsistent repeat capture for construction, maintenance or project communication.Aerial monitoring →
Aerial stills and videoPhotographs or clips from agreed viewpoints, for communication and presentation.Photography & video →

What to expect

Before, during and after capture should stay clear.

The flight is one stage in a simple chain: agree the purpose, capture the brief, then hand over the agreed files.

Agree the brief

Confirm the site, purpose, coverage, intended use and required deliverable.

Capture to the brief

Collect the agreed imagery or data, and tell you about any site condition that changes the plan.

Hand over clearly

Deliver the agreed files and answer any questions about using them.
